title: Demanding more than $250 from Glaser; Red Allen the Uncle Tom
summary: He barged into Glaser's office for money, and says Allen admitted being an Uncle Tom for a dollar.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Just like when I came from Boston and Red wanted me to come back with him. So I called him up and told him what I wanted. 'Can't pay you.'
How much did you tell him you wanted? Do you remember?

... I say, you're going to pay me more than $250 a week. 'Can't do it.' I said, you don't want me. So I walked back in the office one day, he made me so mad. I called him up and his secretary answered the phone. I was broke; I wanted some money. So first the secretary wanted to know who was calling.

So I knew he was there. So she said, "He's not in." I said, "You damn liar, you sea hag!" So I went up there and I kept straight to the back. He said, "You're not supposed to walk in here like that." I said, "Well, she's not supposed to lie to me like that." I said I wanted some money. She said, "Will you please give him a check and let him get out of here?"
Joe Glaser was booking the band at that time?
So then he was handling Louis Armstrong and Red Allen?
Yeah, he always handled Louis Armstrong. So Louis made him what he was to be.
What was his relationship with Red Allen? Did Joe Glaser also like Red Allen?
He and Red got along pretty good 'cause Red admitted he was an Uncle Tom.
He admitted that he was what?
That he was an Uncle Tom?
That's exactly what he said over at the Copper Rail in front of Buster Bailey and me... He said, "I'll admit I'm an Uncle Tom to make a dollar."
